A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same low-rank token-level uncertainty framework, named TokUR in v2. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments on GSM8K, MATH500 and DeepScaleR, including error detection, response selection, particle filtering and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional difficulty-stratified evaluation, baseline comparisons and test-time sampling experiments.

M1.justification: The uncertainty estimator, low-rank perturbation and particle-filter algorithm remain unchanged. The downstream offline selection procedure changes from BoN/WBoN over all candidates to retaining the highest-ranked 10% and applying majority voting or WBoN (Section 4.2.1).

E1.justification: v2 adds a difficulty-stratified math-orz question pool while remaining within mathematical reasoning. The offline selection study drops DeepScaleR, and the online particle-filter study drops GSM8K; both datasets remain evaluated elsewhere.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the evaluated comparators from P(True), predictive entropy and log-likelihood to additionally include Semantic Entropy, SAR, LLM-Check and INSIDE for both Llama models across all three benchmarks. SE and SAR were previously cited but were not evaluated in this comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.2.1 replaces fixed N=16 selection with budgets from 16 to 512, subsampling without replacement from a shared 512-response pool and filtering before aggregation. The new difficulty study uses 500 questions at each of 11 levels defined by Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct failures in ten attempts, evaluated with greedy Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct responses.

E4.justification: v2 replaces the coarse cross-dataset uncertainty mean/variance analysis with difficulty-conditioned uncertainty and error-discrimination analysis, and adds response-budget sensitivity curves. The original GSM8K uncertainty-distribution study moves to Appendix E.1; perturbation-strength, temperature, rejection-threshold and four case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Three-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting remains for detection and particle filtering. The revised offline study introduces ten subsampling repetitions for each N below 512 and reports standard errors in Appendix E.2/Table 4; these repetitions resample a shared response pool.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds comparator results and revises the GSM8K block: for the 1B model, EU/PE AUROCs change from 74.24/72.89 to 65.98/71.21, reversing their reported ranking. Existing MATH500 and DeepScaleR rows remain unchanged. Offline results are replaced by scaling results, and online results also change; unexplained GSM8K revisions and changed selection settings preclude treating these as established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The uncertainty definitions, perturbation equations, independence assumptions, propositions and Appendix C proofs retain the same mathematical substance. Query-level/response-level terminology and revised explanations do not introduce a new theorem, derivation or formal method.

C1.justification: The central training-free uncertainty-estimation contribution remains. The abstract drops v1’s blanket assertion of outperforming existing uncertainty methods and emphasizes scalable test-time reasoning improvement and interpretability, although strong EU-superiority claims remain in the introduction.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the cross-dataset volatility interpretation with an account linking question difficulty, model knowledge and weakened error discrimination on very hard questions. It adds qualifications about external-model assistance and comparator applicability. Appendix B’s limitations remain unchanged, but the new discussion inconsistently calls PE and LL external-model-assisted after classifying them as internal-signal methods.

D1.justification: New Appendix D.2 describes verification-based adaptations of INSIDE, SE and SAR and the reproduced LLM-Check implementation. TokUR hyperparameters, prompts, parsing and vLLM information remain unchanged. v2 removes the explicit 100-question restriction for online MATH500 evaluation without clearly restating that experiment’s sample count.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the new comparators, difficulty dataset and contextual discussion, and Section 5 acknowledges concurrent confidence-based test-time scaling work. Its main positioning as a Bayesian alternative to conventional confidence measures remains unchanged; the duplicate Malinin–Gales references are consolidated.

P1.justification: v2 introduces TokUR naming, rewrites the abstract, revises query/response terminology and reframes generation selection/guidance as offline/online test-time scaling. Preliminary distribution analysis and baseline descriptions move into the appendices, while the overall six-section organization and most methodological prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds difficulty and scaling figures, expands Table 1 with shaded comparator groups, and restructures the offline and online result tables. v1 Figure 1’s left panel becomes standalone appendix Figure 3, while its right panel disappears. Existing ablation, threshold and case-study figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Expanded baselines, difficulty analysis and sampling-budget experiments provide useful additional scrutiny. However, substantial GSM8K result revisions lack an accompanying protocol explanation, retained superiority claims are not uniformly supported by Table 1, and Figure 2 disagrees with Table 4 on GSM8K Pass@1 (43.4% versus 44.43%). These evidential gains and reporting inconsistencies prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
